node.label: Paul Gilroy
node.date_label: 1987: There Ain’t No Black in the Union Jack: The Cultural Politics of Race and Nation · 1993: The Black Atlantic: Modernity and Double Consciousness · 2000: Against Race: Imagining Political Culture Beyond the Color Line
node.description: A cultural theorist and historian of racialized modernity, Black British life and Atlantic diaspora. His Black Atlantic framework crosses national boundaries and treats slavery, music and double consciousness as central to modernity while resisting closed racial identities.
node.representative_figures_and_works: There Ain’t No Black in the Union Jack: The Cultural Politics of Race and Nation (1987); The Black Atlantic: Modernity and Double Consciousness (1993); Against Race: Imagining Political Culture Beyond the Color Line (2000).

proposed_edges.relationship: Uses transnational and intercultural Black Atlantic formations to question national containers for cultural history.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own preface ix–xi read; the framework is explicitly provisional and does not claim complete coverage of Black intellectual history.

proposed_edges.relationship: Criticizes racial purity and closed identity categories while retaining the historical stakes of Black political culture and double consciousness.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own preface ix–xi read, including anti-anti-essentialism; this is not a claim that race has no material consequences or that all identity historians follow Gilroy.
